headline: SILVER SURGES ~5%, GOLD BOUNCES AS DOLLAR SLIDES INTO FOMC WEEK — Oil/Dollar Divergence Fires Both Engines; Gold-Silver Ratio Drops to 68.9
snippet: Silver gained sharply on July 24 as a weaker U.S. dollar and escalating U.S.-Iran trade tensions fired both the monetary and industrial engines simultaneously — the gold-silver ratio falling from 71.1 to 68.9 in a single session as FOMC hold probability sits above 85% ahead of the July 28-29 meeting. With 58% of annual silver demand tied to manufacturing, a simultaneous weakening dollar and surging oil price creates an unusual double-tailwind; mining stocks led the TSX's top percentage gainers as the market repositions out of last week's correction.

headline: CALEDONIA DRILLS 23m AT 2.61 g/t OXIDE AND 16m AT 6.04 g/t SULPHIDE — Blanket Zimbabwe Unveils Brand-New K-Pits Orebody 200m East of Underground; Heap Leach Trial H2 2026 (NYSE: CMCL)
snippet: Caledonia Mining Corp. (NYSE/AIM/VFEX: CMCL) announced July 23 that surface exploration at the K-Pits target on Zimbabwe's Blanket gold mine has outlined an entirely new near-surface gold orebody located approximately 200 metres east of the nearest projected underground workings — oxide intercepts including 23.0m at 2.61 g/t from surface and sulphide intercepts including 16.0m at 6.04 g/t, across 155 RC drill holes (7,063m) and 13 trenches (2,304m). Metallurgical testing for conventional heap leaching shows encouraging initial results; Caledonia plans a 10,000-tonne trial heap leach operation during H2 2026 and an updated Blanket resource statement in August — a potential low-capex, near-term production addition at a mine already producing approximately 75,000–80,000 oz/yr.

headline: OSISKO GOLD VALIDATES CARIBOO LOWHEE RESOURCE MODEL — 185 Holes Confirm Grade Controls; $350M Undrawn Project Loan Conditions Met in Q3 2026 (TSXV: ODV)
snippet: Osisko Gold Group Inc. (TSXV: ODV) released July 23 the final results and reconciliation of its 13,000-metre, 185-hole Lowhee Zone infill program at the Cariboo Gold Project in central British Columbia — with core recovery reaching 94% in 2026 and the program broadly validating and refining the underlying grade model. The milestone directly unlocks value: Appian Capital's technical sign-off, now expected Q3 2026, satisfies conditions precedent for the remaining undrawn US$350 million tranche of Cariboo's senior secured project loan facility, a material de-risking event for what is one of Canada's largest undeveloped gold mine projects.

headline: McFARLANE LAKE JUBY STRIKE EXTENDS TO 1.9KM — 179m AT 0.87 g/t AND 155m AT 0.9 g/t IN NEW HANGING WALL ZONE; Bulk Sample 2027 in Planning (Ontario)
snippet: McFarlane Lake Mining Ltd. reported July 23 additional diamond drill results at the 100%-owned Juby Gold Project west of Gowganda, Ontario — returning wide near-surface intercepts including 179.1m at 0.87 g/t gold and 155m at 0.9 g/t gold from a newly defined hanging wall zone, extending the project's mineralized strike to 1.9 kilometres from a prior 0.75km footprint. A bulk sample is now in planning for 2027 alongside an updated MRE, positioning Juby as a bulk-tonnage open-pit candidate in one of Ontario's historically productive gold belts.

headline: OSISKO METALS GASPÉ COPPER: 320m AT 0.38% Cu FROM 12 NEW HOLES — Porphyry Deepens to 418m Vertical; 25 Intercepts Mix Infill and Step-Out; Resource Upgrade Advancing (TSXV: OM)
snippet: Osisko Metals Inc. (TSXV: OM) announced July 23 new results from the 2026 drill program at the Gaspé Copper Project in Quebec — 25 mineralized intercepts across 12 holes including a 320.5-metre interval averaging 0.38% Cu, with drill hole 30-1199 extending mineralization to 418 metres vertical depth via four intervals of 18–52.5 metres averaging 0.23–0.45% Cu with 2.75–5.32 g/t Ag. The combined infill and step-out program supports both a resource category upgrade and footprint expansion at one of Quebec's most significant copper porphyry systems, advancing the asset toward an economic assessment.

headline: GLADIATOR METALS CUB EAST: 32m AT 1.36% Cu + 0.63 g/t Au INCLUDING 18m AT 2.12% — Yukon Whitehorse Copper Belt High-Grade Continuity Extends 300m Strike; Program Grows to 50,000m (TSXV: GLAD)
snippet: Gladiator Metals Corp. (TSXV: GLAD) reported July 22 assay results from Cub East at its Whitehorse Copper project in Yukon — hole BCG-035 returned 32m at 1.36% Cu, 0.63 g/t Au, and 10.93 g/t Ag including 18m at 2.12% Cu and 1.06 g/t Au, with hole BCG-024 delivering 32.7m at 1.06% Cu and 0.44 g/t Au — extending high-grade mineralization across more than 300 metres of strike. The 2026 drill program has been expanded from 35,000 to more than 50,000 metres, a commitment that underscores operator conviction in the Whitehorse Copper belt as one of Canada's most undervalued critical minerals districts.

headline: GREENLAND MINES ADOPTS POISON PILL AT 15% TRIGGER — 1-Year Rights Plan Signals Unsolicited Bid Pressure on NASDAQ Critical Mineral Explorer (NASDAQ: GRML)
snippet: Greenland Mines Ltd. (NASDAQ: GRML) announced July 23 that its board adopted a limited-duration stockholder rights plan effective July 22, 2026 — a classic poison pill with a 15% ownership trigger and one-year duration expiring July 22, 2027. If triggered, all shareholders except the acquirer may purchase Greenland Mines shares at a 50% discount, rendering hostile takeover economics unworkable. The adoption of unsolicited-bid defences at a Greenland-focused critical minerals explorer, at a time when NATO governments are prioritizing ex-China rare earth and critical mineral supply chains, strongly signals the board is fielding or anticipating acquisition interest.

headline: SHANGHAI COPPER HITS 7-WEEK HIGH AS CHINA SCRAP CRACKDOWN BITES — Yangshan Premium at $103/T; COMEX Within 2% of June All-Time Record Near $6.55/Lb
snippet: Shanghai copper futures rose to a seven-week high driven by Beijing's crackdown on VAT fraud in the copper scrap market — reducing domestic scrap availability and redirecting demand to imported refined metal, pushing the Yangshan copper import premium to $103/tonne (its highest since May 2025) and spot cathode premiums over Shanghai futures to 435 yuan/tonne. In New York, COMEX September copper approached $6.55/lb, within 2% of June's all-time record, as Shanghai Futures Exchange deliverable inventories have been drawn down 82% since early May in one of the fastest warehouse-to-market drawdown sequences ever recorded for a major exchange metal.

headline: CNBC: IRAN ESCALATION COULD FLIP FOMC FROM HOLD TO HIKE — Oil Inflation Path Makes Gold/Silver Rebound 'Potentially Short-Lived'
snippet: A CNBC analysis dated July 23 argues that gold and silver's rebound off multi-month lows could prove short-lived because the same geopolitical catalyst driving safe-haven buying — escalating U.S.-Iran military confrontation through a 12th consecutive night of airstrikes — is simultaneously pushing oil prices higher in a way that feeds into the inflation data set FOMC hawks are watching. The piece maps the specific scenario — a stronger-than-expected CPI print coupled with hawkish language from Fed Chair Warsh — that could reignite the rate-hike trade and restart the correction from January's $5,595 gold peak.

headline: FREEGOLD VENTURES GOLDEN SUMMIT 6-RIG ALASKA CAMPAIGN TIGHTENS PFS FOCUS — 1.48 g/t Au OVER 176.8m INCLUDING 3.09 g/t OVER 45.8m; Starter-Pit Grade Confidence Targeted (TSX: FVL)
snippet: Freegold Ventures Ltd. (TSX: FVL) released additional drill results from the Dolphin Area of its Golden Summit gold project in Alaska as six rigs advance infill drilling, metallurgical testing, and technical studies to underpin a 2027 Pre-Feasibility Study — with hole GS2622 returning 176.8 metres at 1.48 g/t Au from 389.2 metres including 45.8 metres at 3.09 g/t Au, adding to the 17.2-million-ounce resource. The 2026 program's mandate has shifted from discovery drilling to identifying the highest-grade starter-pit candidate within the broader deposit — a PFS-focused signal that Freegold is engineering toward the lowest practical capital intensity at first production.

headline: MINERS vs. BULLION: GDX/GDXJ DELIVERED 79% MORE UPSIDE — But 10% Monthly Gold Drop Produced 'Bloodbath' in Equities; Which ETF Is Right for the Second Half?
snippet: A Motley Fool analysis published July 21 quantifies the leverage trade-off for retail gold investors: GDX and GDXJ have delivered 79% more upside than physical gold bullion over the past year's bull run, but gold mining equities have also suffered brutal downside magnification in corrections — the recent 10% monthly gold decline translating to a sector-wide bloodbath. The piece concludes junior miners (GDXJ) remain the best asymmetric vehicle for investors who can tolerate volatility and seek leveraged participation, while physical gold ETFs better suit those whose primary objective is capital preservation rather than amplified exposure to the gold price.
